paper_title: Efficiency Limits and Color of Semitransparent Organic Solar Cells for Application in Building-Integrated Photovoltaics

knowledge_points.content: The maximum achievable efficiency of semitransparent organic solar cells is intrinsically linked to the specific shape of the External Quantum Efficiency (EQE) spectrum and the target transparency level.
knowledge_points.evidence: Figure S1. EQE shapes that correspond to the maximum efficiencies for some of the transparency values shown in Figure 2.

knowledge_points.content: The CIE 1931 color space is used as a standard framework to calculate and visualize the color coordinates of semitransparent organic solar cells based on their spectral response.
knowledge_points.evidence: Figure S4. Color coordinates in the CIE 1931 color space calculated for the model of constant EQE.

knowledge_points.content: For a fixed transparency of 10%, the band gap (Eg) of the organic semiconductor material is a primary determinant of the x- and y-color coordinates in the CIE 1931 chromaticity diagram.
knowledge_points.evidence: Figure S5. Band gap Eg (a) ... plotted over x- and y- color coordinates for a transparency of 10%.

knowledge_points.content: The width of the External Quantum Efficiency spectrum (Δλ) directly influences the resulting color coordinates of semitransparent organic solar cells at a given transparency level.
knowledge_points.evidence: Figure S5. ... EQE width Δλ (b) plotted over x- and y- color coordinates for a transparency of 10%.

knowledge_points.content: Efficiency limits and color performance of semitransparent organic solar cells can be predicted using a model of constant External Quantum Efficiency (EQE) across the absorption range.
knowledge_points.evidence: Figure S4. Color coordinates in the CIE 1931 color space calculated for the model of constant EQE.

knowledge_points.content: Building-Integrated Photovoltaics (BIPV) applications require a balance between the power conversion efficiency of the solar cell and its aesthetic properties, such as transparency and color neutrality.
knowledge_points.evidence: Efficiency Limits and Color of Semitransparent Organic Solar Cells for Application in Building-Integrated Photovoltaics

knowledge_points.content: The study identifies specific EQE shapes that maximize efficiency for various transparency values, indicating that spectral engineering is required to reach the thermodynamic limits of ST-OSCs.
knowledge_points.evidence: Figure S2. EQE shapes that correspond to the maximum efficiencies for some of the transparency values shown in Figure 3.

knowledge_points.content: A transparency value of 10% is used as a benchmark to analyze how the physical parameters of the photoactive layer, specifically band gap and absorption width, dictate the visual appearance of the device.
knowledge_points.evidence: Figure S5. Band gap Eg (a) and EQE width Δλ (b) plotted over x- and y- color coordinates for a transparency of 10%.
